title: Laser Lords (USA)
symptom: Shot-dependent black/white and magenta/green line patterns appear along the bottom of the post-logo video and crossfade with each shot; later menu/gameplay screens may also appear overscanned
expected: Decoded video and base graphics follow the authored source and live hardware aperture without exposing unintended final-line data or clipping authored edges

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: The non-DVC post-logo sequence uses Green Book QHY real-time video. An incorrect decoded height, destination stride, or final partial update exposes source-dependent data along the last displayed row.
supporting_evidence: The disc inventory identifies QHY Form-2 real-time video rather than MPEG.
The line patterns change with each shot and participate in crossfades, tying them to source/drawmap updates rather than a static frontend border.
contradicting_evidence: Kether Europe shows the same content-correlated bottom-line symptom using CLUT8/RL7/DYUV rather than QHY, so QHY decoding alone cannot explain the shared defect.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Capture the final source QHY line, PCL destination, completed drawmap, individual MCD212 plane, composed raster, and frontend output. If the artifact first appears only after the drawmap stage, source decode/stride is not the cause.
citations: Green Book Release 2 real-time video and QHY coding

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: The title's display control program or the emulator's MCD212 line/mask boundary exposes one row beyond the intended drawmap.
supporting_evidence: The patterns are confined to the bottom edge.
Later base-graphics screens also appear to lose edge content.
Kether Europe shows the same content-correlated bottom line using CLUT8/RL7/DYUV rather than QHY, which points to a shared downstream display boundary.
contradicting_evidence: The pattern colors track video shot changes, so the source may already contain the bad row.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Compare the final drawmap row with the plane and hardware raster. Identical artifacts in the drawmap falsify a composition-only explanation.
citations: MCD212 specification display-file and DCA line boundaries

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: The global Typical CRT aperture may be cropping screens 3 and 4 differently from the intended analog viewing area, independently of the QHY bottom-row artifact.
supporting_evidence: Screens 3 and 4 show text and graphics touching or crossing the visible edges.
contradicting_evidence: No real-hardware comparison or Full signal capture is recorded yet.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Capture the same stable screens using Full signal and Typical CRT. If Full signal already lacks the edge content, frontend aperture selection is not causal.
citations: Philips TN 093 image-format and safe-area guidance

manual_verification.notes: User screenshots reproduce shot-dependent bottom-row patterns during QHY video and possible edge clipping in later screens. A future pass should compare the same stable frames under Full signal and Typical CRT and capture the six display-provenance stages.

Kether Europe reproduces a content-correlated bottom artifact line with CLUT8/RL7/DYUV RTF data. This weakens a QHY-only explanation and raises common RTF destination/drawmap or MCD212 lower-boundary handling.
